## Next-month stock returns {#sec-bem-returns}

Start with eligible common stocks at the end of month $t$ and look up the
return for the same security in month $t+1$. Do not require it to remain in the
common-stock universe in the holding month: that would screen out delistings.

Chapter 7 uses the legacy CRSP delisting return in place of the regular monthly
return if the stock delists. If no delisting return is recorded, it imputes a
loss of 30% for the codes listed below and a loss of 100% for other delistings.
This is the book's convention for legacy data, not a reason to adjust the
reported returns from CRSP CIZ a second time.

```{python}
first_return = pl.date(1926, 7, 1)
first_return_late = pl.date(1963, 7, 1)
hold_month = pl.col("month").dt.offset_by("1mo")

delist = (
    load_parquet("msedelist", "crsp")
    .with_columns(month=pl.col("dlstdt").dt.month_start())
    .filter(pl.col("month").is_between(first_return, last))
    .select("permno", "month", "dlret", "dlstcd")
)
poor_performance = (
    pl.col("dlstcd").is_in([500, 520, 580, 584])
    | pl.col("dlstcd").is_between(551, 574)
)
imputed_delist = pl.when(poor_performance).then(-0.30).otherwise(-1.00)

return_panel = (
    universe
    .with_columns(formation_month="month")
    .with_columns(month=hold_month)
    .filter(pl.col("month").is_between(first_return, last))
    .drop("ret")
    .join(
        msf.select("permno", "month", ret_raw="ret"),
        on=["permno", "month"], how="left", validate="1:1",
    )
    .join(delist, on=["permno", "month"], how="left", validate="1:1")
    .join(factors.select("month", "rf"), on="month", how="left", validate="m:1")
    .with_columns(
        ret_adj=pl.when(pl.col("dlstcd").is_not_null())
        .then(pl.coalesce("dlret", imputed_delist))
        .otherwise(pl.col("ret_raw"))
    )
    .with_columns(
        excess_raw=pl.col("ret_raw") - pl.col("rf"),
        excess_adj=pl.col("ret_adj") - pl.col("rf"),
    )
)
```

The Fama–French risk-free return applies to the holding month, not the
formation month. We first calculate the statistics across stocks for each
return month, then average those monthly statistics. In particular, the means
give each month equal weight, irrespective of the number of stocks in that
month. We use sample standard deviations, bias-adjusted skewness and
excess kurtosis, and linearly interpolated quantiles.

```{python}
def summarize_returns(start):
    x = pl.col("return_pct")
    return (
        return_panel
        .filter(pl.col("month") >= start)
        .select("month", "excess_adj", "ret_adj", "excess_raw", "ret_raw")
        .unpivot(index="month", variable_name="series", value_name="return_pct")
        .with_columns(return_pct=100 * x)
        .group_by("month", "series")
        .agg(
            n=x.count(),
            mean=x.mean(),
            sd=x.std(),
            skew=x.skew(bias=False),
            excess_kurtosis=x.kurtosis(fisher=True, bias=False),
            min=x.min(),
            p05=x.quantile(0.05, interpolation="linear"),
            p25=x.quantile(0.25, interpolation="linear"),
            median=x.median(),
            p75=x.quantile(0.75, interpolation="linear"),
            p95=x.quantile(0.95, interpolation="linear"),
            max=x.max(),
        )
        .group_by("series")
        .agg(pl.exclude("month", "series").mean())
        .collect()
    )

def display_returns(table):
    labels = {
        "excess_adj": "Adjusted excess",
        "ret_adj": "Adjusted total",
        "excess_raw": "Unadjusted excess",
        "ret_raw": "Unadjusted total",
    }
    return (
        table
        .with_columns(series=pl.col("series").replace_strict(labels))
        .unpivot(index="series", variable_name="statistic", value_name="value")
        .pivot(on="series", index="statistic", values="value")
        .select("statistic", *labels.values())
        .with_columns(pl.exclude("statistic").round(2))
    )

table_7_2 = summarize_returns(first_return)
table_7_3 = summarize_returns(first_return_late)
```

### July 1926–December 2012 (Table 7.2)

```{python}
#| echo: false

with pl.Config(tbl_rows=12):
    display(display_returns(table_7_2))
```

### July 1963–December 2012 (Table 7.3)

```{python}
#| echo: false

with pl.Config(tbl_rows=12):
    display(display_returns(table_7_3))
```

On the local vintage, average adjusted excess returns are 0.96% and 0.74%
per month for the two samples, versus 0.96% and 0.75% in the book. We get
about 3,111 and 4,780 valid adjusted returns per month, versus 3,112 and
4,782. The upper tail is less close: the average monthly maximum adjusted
excess return is 191.10% and 273.12%, against 208.10% and 302.74% in the
book. The unadjusted maxima round to 186.78% and 266.66%, against 186.80%
and 266.66% in the book. That points toward a difference in the delisting
observations rather than a general shift in ordinary returns, but we cannot
identify those observations without the original data and code.

```{python}
#| include: false

return_months = (
    return_panel
    .group_by("month")
    .agg(
        has_rf=pl.col("rf").is_not_null().all(),
        adjusted=pl.col("ret_adj").count(),
    )
    .collect()
)
assert return_months.height == 1038
assert return_months["has_rf"].all()
assert (return_months["adjusted"] > 0).all()
```
